boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Northeast Philadelphia campus destinations for studying, collaborating, recreation, reflection, and everyday student support.

cards.title: University Library
cards.subtitle: Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Set up with research help, computers, printers, Wi-Fi, and individual study rooms; use the listed library hours before making it your work stop.
cards.short_summary: A campus library equipped for research and individual study.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family University says its Library provides librarians, Tiger Wi-Fi, computers, printers, individual study rooms, and academic resources.
cards.source_title: Library | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Library services and hours are published by the University; check the current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Center for Teaching and Learning
cards.subtitle: University Library, Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Use the modular seating when you need to switch between solo work, tutoring, a group project, or a short reset between classes.
cards.short_summary: Flexible work and tutoring space inside the University Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family identifies the Center for Teaching and Learning as a space with modular seating for individual and group work, tutoring, group work, and regrouping.
cards.source_title: Commuting to Campus | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Located in the University Library according to the 2026 campus map.

cards.title: Campus Center
cards.subtitle: Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Choose a common-area seat near the bookstore, Dining Commons, or exterior deck when you want to meet, study, or sit outdoors in warm weather.
cards.short_summary: A central building with designated common-area study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family lists study areas outside its bookstore, in Student Affairs, beside the Dining Commons, and on the Campus Center exterior deck.
cards.source_title: Commuting to Campus | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: The University identifies these as Campus Center common areas; availability may vary with building operations.

cards.title: Education and Technology Center
cards.subtitle: Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Head to the ETC common areas for a change of study setting, or use its computer labs and teaching-focused spaces when they fit your work.
cards.short_summary: A campus academic building with common areas and computer labs.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family lists Education and Technology Center common areas as a campus study option and maps computer labs and an auditorium there.
cards.source_title: Commuting to Campus | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: The campus map places the ETC on the Northeast Philadelphia campus; access to specific rooms can depend on scheduling.

cards.title: Library Huddle Rooms
cards.subtitle: University Library lower level, Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Reserve a room through the Library front desk for a project session; each room has a large monitor to support in-person or remote collaboration.
cards.short_summary: Bookable small-group rooms designed for collaborative project work.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family reports eight huddle spaces on the Campus Library lower level, each with a large monitor; students can book them for up to two hours.
cards.source_title: Huddle Room Study Spaces Open in Campus Library | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Book through the Library front desk; the University says a waiting list is used when rooms are occupied.

cards.title: Gallagher Family Center
cards.subtitle: University Library, Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Use the campus map to find this named Library destination, then check locally for its current programming, seating, or access arrangements.
cards.short_summary: A named student-facing destination in the University Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family's 2026 campus map lists the Gallagher Family Center among the destinations in the University Library.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Philadelphia Campus Map 2026
cards.access_notes: Located in the University Library on the official campus map; confirm current use or availability on arrival.

cards.title: Arcade
cards.subtitle: University Library, Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Find the Arcade through the University Library and use it as a named indoor stop between classes; confirm current availability when you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A named recreation-oriented destination mapped inside the Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family's 2026 campus map lists an Arcade in the University Library.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Philadelphia Campus Map 2026
cards.access_notes: Located in the University Library on the official campus map; confirm current access with Library staff.

cards.title: Makerspace
cards.subtitle: University Library, Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Locate the Makerspace in the Library when a project calls for a designated making environment, then ask staff about current equipment and use procedures.
cards.short_summary: A named makerspace destination mapped in the Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family's 2026 campus map lists a Makerspace in the University Library.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Philadelphia Campus Map 2026
cards.access_notes: Located in the University Library on the official campus map; verify available equipment and access procedures locally.

cards.title: Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: University Library, Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Use the official map to locate the Fitness Center, then check with campus staff for current entry requirements and operating arrangements.
cards.short_summary: A named fitness destination on the University Library map listing.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family's 2026 campus map lists a Fitness Center among the destinations in the University Library.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Philadelphia Campus Map 2026
cards.access_notes: The official campus map places the Fitness Center in the University Library; confirm current access before visiting.

cards.title: Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Northeast Philadelphia campus
cards.notes: Make this named campus stop part of a quiet reflection break, and look for it on the official map before heading out across campus.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor-oriented reflection destination on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family's 2026 campus map lists a Labyrinth on its Northeast Philadelphia campus.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Philadelphia Campus Map 2026
cards.access_notes: Locate it with the official campus map; outdoor conditions and campus operations may affect access.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-purchase activities and student resources at Holy Family University, with access limits noted.

cards.title: Queue up at the Esports Center
cards.subtitle: Holy Family University Esports Center
cards.notes: Submit the access request, then meet friends during open hours for a no-purchase session on the center’s gaming PCs.
cards.short_summary: A campus gaming session with access approval.
cards.evidence_claim: All Holy Family students can use the Esports Center during free hours; it has 20 PCs and lists League of Legends, Valorant, and Rocket League.
cards.source_title: Esports | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Current Holy Family students must submit the Esports Room Access Request Form. Listed hours are 10 a.m.–midnight daily; closed for varsity practices and matches.

cards.entity_name: Holy Family University Distinguished Writers Series public reading
cards.title: Attend a Distinguished Writers reading
cards.subtitle: Holy Family University campus
cards.notes: Check the series schedule and bring a friend to a public reading; the university describes these readings as free.
cards.short_summary: Free public readings with visiting writers and scholars.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family University states that its Distinguished Writers Series brings visiting authors and scholars to campus for free, public readings each academic year.
cards.source_title: Our Community | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Events are scheduled by the series; confirm the current program, date, and location before going.

cards.title: Start a free Tutor.com session
cards.subtitle: Online through a Holy Family course Canvas shell
cards.notes: Open Tutor.com from Canvas and work through a question or draft with a tutor; invite a classmate to tackle similar work nearby.
cards.short_summary: On-demand academic help that students can use online.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family offers free on-demand online tutoring through Tutor.com, including one-on-one help and writing-review requests.
cards.source_title: Tutor.com Resources | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Access it through the Tutor.com link in the relevant Canvas course shell. The university says tutors are available 24/7.

cards.entity_name: Holy Family University Library study rooms
cards.title: Plan a study-room meetup
cards.subtitle: University Library, Philadelphia Campus
cards.notes: Coordinate a focused group session in a study room, then use the library’s research help and academic resources as needed.
cards.short_summary: A campus library setting for collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists individual study rooms, computers, Tiger Wi‑Fi, librarians, and academic resources for Holy Family students.
cards.source_title: Library | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Holy Family students have access to the library building, collection, and services. Check the library page for current operating hours.

cards.title: Take a quiet break in the Zen Den
cards.subtitle: Center for Wellness and Spirituality, Delaney Hall
cards.notes: Use the Zen Den for a low-key reset between classes; keep the visit quiet so others can use the mindfulness space too.
cards.short_summary: A designated campus space for mindfulness and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family describes the Zen Den as a campus space created to encourage students’ mental health, mindfulness, and relaxation.
cards.source_title: The Center for Wellness and Spirituality | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Located on the ground floor of Delaney Hall as part of the Center for Wellness and Spirituality; availability may vary.

cards.title: Visit the Essential Needs Pantry
cards.subtitle: Center for Wellness and Spirituality, Delaney Hall
cards.notes: If you need essentials, check in with the pantry and take what supports your week; it provides food, hygiene items, and supplies.
cards.short_summary: A campus resource for free food, toiletries, and school supplies.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family says its Essential Needs Pantry gives college students free access to basic requirements, including food, toiletries, and certain supplies.
cards.source_title: The Center for Wellness and Spirituality | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: The page identifies this as a campus resource in the Center for Wellness and Spirituality on Delaney Hall’s ground floor.

cards.title: Book a Counseling Services visit
cards.subtitle: Counseling Services, Delaney Hall Room 102
cards.notes: Schedule an appointment when you want confidential support or help building coping skills; use the listed contact details to begin.
cards.short_summary: Confidential short-term counseling for eligible students.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family states that Counseling Services are free and confidential for currently enrolled full-time students, with part-time eligibility at the director’s discretion.
cards.source_title: Counseling Services | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Appointments are listed Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m., in Delaney Hall Room 102. This is a private support service, not a social event.

cards.title: Use the Health Services resource
cards.subtitle: Holy Family University Health Services
cards.notes: Reach out when you need basic medical support or health education; the university identifies the service as free and confidential.
cards.short_summary: No-cost basic medical care and health education for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family says Health Services provides students free, confidential access to basic medical care, including assessments, diagnostic testing, referrals, and education.
cards.source_title: Health & Wellness | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Use the university’s Health Services link to confirm current appointment and access procedures. This is an individual health resource.

cards.title: Handle laundry at Delaney Hall
cards.subtitle: Delaney Hall Residence, Philadelphia Campus
cards.notes: Residents can pair laundry with a casual catch-up in the hall’s shared areas; bring your own detergent and follow residence access rules.
cards.short_summary: A residence-hall laundry option with free machines.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family lists a laundry room with free washers and dryers among Delaney Hall Residence amenities.
cards.source_title: Residence Halls at Holy Family University | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: For Delaney Hall residents; the building uses swipe-card access and has 24-hour security monitoring.

cards.title: Ride the Newtown West Shuttle
cards.subtitle: Departs from the Campus Center Lot, Philadelphia Campus
cards.notes: Meet at the Campus Center Lot and ride with classmates to the Newtown West campus when the academic-term schedule is running.
cards.short_summary: A free intercampus shuttle for Holy Family students.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family states that the Newtown West Shuttle is free for students, staff, and faculty traveling between the Philadelphia and Newtown West campuses.
cards.source_title: Newtown West Shuttle Schedule | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Pickup is at the Philadelphia Campus Center Lot. Service runs Monday–Thursday when classes are in session; check the posted schedule before departure.

warnings: Several cards are student services or student-access spaces rather than public social venues; access requirements are stated in each card.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Philadelphia-campus places for individual work, group work, research, tutoring, or computer-based coursework.

cards.title: Holy Family University Library
cards.subtitle: Philadelphia campus library
cards.notes: Start at the library for a general study session, then use its Wi-Fi, computers, printing, or an individual study room as needed.
cards.short_summary: A campus library base with individual study rooms and academic technology.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family says its Philadelphia library provides Wi-Fi, computers, printers, and individual study rooms.
cards.source_title: Library | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Holy Family students, faculty, instructors, and staff have access; consult the library page for current hours.

cards.title: Huddle Room Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: University Library lower level
cards.notes: For a project meeting, ask at the library front desk to book one of the lower-level huddle rooms for up to two hours.
cards.short_summary: Eight library huddle spaces equipped with large monitor screens for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family documents eight lower-level library huddle spaces with large monitors; students can book a room for up to two hours through the front desk.
cards.source_title: Huddle Room Study Spaces Open in Campus Library | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Book through the Library front desk; the documented maximum reservation is two hours.

cards.entity_name: Holy Family University Archives Reading Room
cards.title: University Archives Reading Room
cards.subtitle: University Library upper level
cards.notes: Bring a defined research question and contact the archivist ahead of time to arrange access to the Archives reading room.
cards.short_summary: A designated reading room for researching Holy Family University history and publications.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family says the Archives Room is a work room and reading room for researchers, and recommends scheduling with the archivist in advance.
cards.source_title: University Archives | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Available to the University community and people with a legitimate research interest; call ahead because hours depend on archivist availability.

cards.title: Center for Academic Enhancement
cards.subtitle: University Library, second floor
cards.notes: Schedule a tutoring-focused work block in the CAE, located in the library’s Center for Teaching & Learning on the second floor.
cards.short_summary: A library-based academic-support setting with professional and peer tutoring.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family identifies the CAE on the second floor of the University Library and says its services are offered at no cost to students.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University’s Center for Academic Enhancement Awarded College Reading and Learning Association Tutor Certification | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: The University says CAE services are provided at no cost; check its tutoring system for appointment availability.

cards.entity_name: Holy Family Hall Room 204 Computer Lab
cards.title: Holy Family Hall Room 204 Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Holy Family Hall, Room 204

cards.notes: Use this documented ETC lab for focused computer coursework, and check the open-lab posting before making it your work location.

cards.notes: Set up in this listed ETC computer lab for digital assignments, after confirming the room’s posted open-laboratory availability.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Follow Grant Avenue from Holy Family’s Frankford Avenue campus for practical stops: groceries, meals, errands, movement, care, and a riverfront historic site.

cards.title: Stock the grocery list
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 2550 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Use this Grant Avenue stop for groceries, pharmacy needs, or prepared-food counter options before returning to campus.
cards.short_summary: A full grocery and pharmacy stop on Grant Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: GIANT lists its store at 2550 Grant Ave with grocery departments, a pharmacy, and pickup and delivery services.
cards.source_title: GIANT at 2550 Grant Ave Philadelphia, PA
cards.access_notes: Retail store; purchase required for goods and services.

cards.title: Plan a platter stop
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 2550 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Order a chicken, beef gyro, or falafel platter from the listed Grant Avenue location and check its current hours first.
cards.short_summary: A counter-service meal option at the Grant Avenue shopping center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Halal Guys lists a Philadelphia location at 2550 Grant Ave and identifies chicken, beef gyro, and falafel menu options.
cards.source_title: The Halal Guys — Philadelphia, 2550 Grant Ave
cards.access_notes: Food purchase required; official location page lists daily hours through 11 PM.

cards.title: Pick up a pizza
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 2550 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s own menu to choose a pizza or stromboli, and note that the business says it accepts cash only.
cards.short_summary: A long-running pizza counter sharing the Grant Avenue address.
cards.evidence_claim: Vince's Pizzeria identifies its 2550 Grant Avenue location, pizza and stromboli menu, and cash-only payment policy.
cards.source_title: Vince's Pizzeria
cards.access_notes: Food purchase required; bring cash as stated by the business.

cards.title: Know the urgent-care address
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 2451 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Save this nearby care location for a non-emergency health need; call ahead or use Jefferson’s location details before visiting.
cards.short_summary: A named Jefferson urgent-care location on Grant Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson Health lists Grant Avenue – JeffExpress Urgent Care at 2451 Grant Avenue in Philadelphia and notes public transportation and wheelchair access.
cards.source_title: Jefferson Health imaging and radiology locations
cards.access_notes: Medical services and coverage may involve charges; use for appropriate urgent-care needs, not emergencies.

cards.title: Choose tacos or a quesadilla
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 3180 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s menu before heading over; it lists tacos, burritos, fajitas, quesadillas, desserts, and takeout.
cards.short_summary: A Mexican restaurant directly on the Grant Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Don Panchito Mexican Grill lists its restaurant at 3180 Grant Ave and describes Mexican dishes including tacos, burritos, fajitas, and quesadillas.
cards.source_title: Don Panchito Mexican Grill
cards.access_notes: Food purchase required; verify current service details with the restaurant.

cards.title: Grab coffee or breakfast
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 3320 Grant Ave, Unit 18B
cards.notes: Use mobile ordering or stop in for coffee and donuts; the official listing also notes free Wi-Fi at this location.
cards.short_summary: A coffee-and-donut stop with mobile ordering on Grant Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Dunkin' lists its 3320 Grant Ave, Unit 18B location with mobile ordering, free Wi-Fi, and daily operating hours.
cards.source_title: Dunkin' at 3320 Grant Ave in Philadelphia
cards.access_notes: Purchase required for food and drinks; official hours vary by day.

cards.title: Handle a banking errand
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 3330 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Use this full-service PFFCU branch for a banking errand; confirm membership and service requirements before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A credit-union branch at Grant Avenue and Academy Road.
cards.evidence_claim: PFFCU lists its Grant and Academy Branch at 3330 Grant Avenue and places it in the shopping center at Grant Avenue and Academy Road.
cards.source_title: PFFCU Grant and Academy Branch
cards.access_notes: Banking destination; account eligibility and transaction terms apply.

cards.title: Book a movement class
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 3360 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Review the class schedule and book ahead for heated or non-heated yoga, Pilates, or restorative movement at this studio.
cards.short_summary: A Grant Avenue studio offering yoga, Pilates, and restorative classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Den Philly identifies its studio at 3360 Grant Avenue and states that its instructors teach heated and non-heated yoga, Pilates, and restorative classes.
cards.source_title: The Den Philly — About
cards.access_notes: Class booking and payment are required; review the studio schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Cover small supply needs
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 3366 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Use this specific Grant Avenue store for low-cost household, school, or snack items when a full grocery stop is unnecessary.
cards.short_summary: A named discount-retail stop directly on Grant Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Dollar Tree lists a store at 3366 Grant Avenue in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania 19114.
cards.source_title: Dollar Tree Store at Grant Avenue in Philadelphia, PA
cards.access_notes: Retail store; purchase required for goods.

cards.title: Visit the riverfront estate
cards.subtitle: Grant Avenue corridor — 5001 Grant Ave
cards.notes: Follow Glen Foerd’s directions to the historic riverfront site, then consult its visitor information for current public programs and access.
cards.short_summary: A historic cultural destination at the eastern end of Grant Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Glen Foerd lists its address as 5001 Grant Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19114; Riverfront North identifies it as the northern extent of its park-and-trail network.
cards.source_title: Glen Foerd — Directions
cards.access_notes: Check Glen Foerd’s current visitor and event information before traveling; some programs may require registration or admission.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Holy Family University traditions, ceremonies, and recurring campus practices.

cards.title: Christmas Rose
cards.subtitle: Holiday tradition since 1954
cards.notes: Look for the Christmas Rose archive page’s decade-by-decade photos and read how the holiday gathering has changed while continuing on campus.
cards.short_summary: A Holy Family holiday gathering rooted in a 1954 celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family says Christmas Rose has been celebrated since 1954 and remains one of its longest-standing traditions.
cards.source_title: Christmas Rose at Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: See the university’s current events communications for attendance details.

cards.entity_name: First-Year Student Convocation and Block Party
cards.title: First-Year Student Convocation and Block Party
cards.subtitle: August welcome ceremony and gathering
cards.notes: New students can watch for the formal convocation and the following Welcome Back Block Party listed in the student handbook each August.
cards.short_summary: Holy Family marks the incoming first-year class with a ceremony and campus gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family’s student handbook describes First-Year Student Convocation as celebrating the entering class, followed by a Welcome Back Block Party.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Student Handbook 2024–2025
cards.access_notes: Scheduled in August; consult current university announcements for details.

cards.title: Constitution Day
cards.subtitle: Annual civic-learning celebration
cards.notes: Check the fall calendar for Constitution Day programming, which the handbook frames around the Constitution’s history and civic engagement.
cards.short_summary: An annual Holy Family program focused on constitutional history and civic engagement.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family’s student handbook calls Constitution Day an annual celebration on all campuses with programming on the Constitution’s history and civic engagement.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Student Handbook 2024–2025
cards.access_notes: Held annually; format and location can vary by year.

cards.title: Opening Mass and SGA Blessing
cards.subtitle: August faith celebration
cards.notes: Students interested in the faith-life calendar can look for Opening Mass, when Student Government Association officers are sworn in and blessed.
cards.short_summary: A Catholic Mass that also marks the start of the SGA year.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family’s student handbook says Opening Mass includes the swearing-in and blessing of Student Government Association officials.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Student Handbook 2024–2025
cards.access_notes: A faith-based opportunity; check current campus ministry and student-life notices.

cards.title: Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Students and alumni share campus life
cards.notes: Watch for fall Homecoming announcements if you want a campus event designed to bring students and guests together with alumni.
cards.short_summary: A fall gathering connecting current students with Holy Family alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family’s student handbook describes Homecoming as an event where students and guests experience campus life with alumni.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Student Handbook 2024–2025
cards.access_notes: Typically listed for September or October; consult current Homecoming information.

cards.entity_name: Great Day to be a Tiger Charter Celebration
cards.title: Great Day to be a Tiger
cards.subtitle: February 11 charter anniversary
cards.notes: Join the February charter anniversary observance for its Mass of Thanksgiving and birthday party, as described in the student handbook.
cards.short_summary: Holy Family’s annual celebration of its Pennsylvania charter date.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family’s student handbook states that February 11, its Commonwealth of Pennsylvania charter date, is celebrated with a Mass of Thanksgiving and birthday party.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Student Handbook 2024–2025
cards.access_notes: Occurs in February; check the current calendar for program details.

cards.title: Big Cat Block Party
cards.subtitle: Annual end-of-year outdoor fair
cards.notes: Save the spring date for the annual outdoor fair, presented by Student Engagement and Student Government with food and games.
cards.short_summary: A spring end-of-year fair organized through campus student-life offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family’s student handbook identifies the Big Cat Block Party as its annual end-of-year outdoor fair with food and games.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Student Handbook 2024–2025
cards.access_notes: Held in April according to the handbook; event specifics vary annually.

cards.title: Late Night Champions
cards.subtitle: Finals-week breakfast tradition
cards.notes: During finals week, check student-event notices for this early-week decompression program built around late-night breakfast foods.
cards.short_summary: A finals-week tradition offering a break before exams.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family’s student handbook calls Late Night Champions a tradition at the beginning of each fall and spring finals week featuring late-night breakfast foods.
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Student Handbook 2024–2025
cards.access_notes: Held at the start of fall and spring finals weeks; the handbook does not provide current event hours.

cards.title: Teneor Votis
cards.subtitle: Holy Family’s motto
cards.notes: Notice the Latin motto in university materials and connect it to the handbook’s interpretation: giving in return for what one has received.
cards.short_summary: A Latin motto that expresses Holy Family’s sense of responsibility and service.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family’s handbook identifies Teneor Votis as the university motto, translating it as “I am bound by my responsibilities.”
cards.source_title: Holy Family University Student Handbook 2024–2025
cards.access_notes: A university motto rather than a scheduled event.

cards.title: Folio Literary Magazine
cards.subtitle: Creative-work tradition since 1959
cards.notes: Browse the university’s Folio information and look for calls for creative work if you want to follow this long-running campus publication.
cards.short_summary: Holy Family’s literary magazine, carrying student and community creativity across decades.
cards.evidence_claim: Holy Family says Folio has served as its literary magazine since 1959 and describes it as a lasting tradition.
cards.source_title: News & Media | Holy Family University
cards.access_notes: Check the Folio section or university communications for submission and publication information.
